heroHeadline: PLA 24 Sorties May 20 (13 Cross N/C/SW/E ADIZ — Largest Post-Summit Surge); 7 Sorties May 21; Taiwan Cabinet Approves NT$295B Procurement Budget; HIMARS Deadline 10 Days
heroSubtitle: PLA activity on May 20 surged to 24 aircraft sorties — 13 crossing the median line into northern, central, southwestern, and eastern ADIZ sectors simultaneously — the largest single-day post-summit sortie count and the broadest multi-sector incursion since the May 7 surge (22 sorties). Six PLAN vessels and 3 official ships also operated around Taiwan, the highest official ship count of the post-summit period. The 4-sector simultaneous penetration geometry (N+C+SW+E) mirrors PLA blockade rehearsal patterns. Activity stepped back to 7 sorties on May 21 (6 crossing the median line, 7 PLAN vessels + 1 official ship), consistent with the established spike-then-pullback oscillation pattern. On the same day as the May 20 PLA surge, Taiwan's Cabinet approved a NT$295 billion (~US$9.3 billion) special military procurement budget covering HIMARS launchers and munitions, M109A7 self-propelled howitzers, Javelin anti-tank missiles, TOW 2B anti-armor missiles, and anti-armor drone missile systems. The HIMARS payment deadline is May 31, now 10 days away. Taiwan's Minister of National Defense Wellington Koo confirmed on May 21 that if the Legislative Yuan fails to pass the budget before May 31, the Executive Yuan will invoke Article 84 of the Budget Act to authorize emergency payment — a legally available but politically contentious fallback. The Legislative Yuan Finance Committee has scheduled hearings for Monday with a floor vote expected Wednesday-Thursday. The full May 2026 PLA sortie sequence: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7→13→24→7.
